card_overview_title.title:
Diff, validate and label
circuit-tracer circuits
card_overview_title.body: Attribution graphs show where influence flows. circuitkit asks what training changed, whether the features cause the behaviour, and what each feature does.

card_overview_end.title: pip install steerlab-circuitkit
card_overview_end.body: Docs, notebooks and the five-minute quickstart: github.com/albertlieyingadrian/steerlab · packages/circuitkit

card_validate_title.title: Switch or readout?
card_validate_title.body: A graph ranks features by influence. The validator switches them off, pushes them and patches them, each against random and size-matched controls.

card_validate_end.title: The RL hack's top features are readouts
card_validate_end.body: Run live on the Pigment Gym RL checkpoint of Qwen3-1.7B, the graph's ten features, together and one by one, come back as readouts, as in the episode. See examples/data/live/.

card_diff_title.title: What did training change?
card_diff_title.body: Compare attribution graphs of the same prompts before and after fine-tuning or RL, with a random null, a stability check and a validity check.

card_diff_end.title: Same ten features as the study
card_diff_end.body: 9 of 10 specific to the run that hacked, 6 replicated in another seed, reconstruction error unchanged by RL. Caveat built in: the transcoders were trained on the base model.

card_labels_title.title: Cheap labels you can check
card_labels_title.body: Claude Haiku 5.5 labels each feature from its top examples; a detector then scores the label on held-out examples it never saw.

card_labels_end.title: Neuronpedia-level labels for $0.26
card_labels_end.body: 50 Gemma-2-2B features: detection AUROC 0.80 (Neuronpedia: 0.78 / 0.80), simulation r 0.45 (0.37 / 0.38). Every reply cached; export in Neuronpedia's format.
